1: * Task finder - Find common store changes by task and open the matching guide or settings. Browsing the task finder is read-only. Each task identifies the specific change it saves and any separate activation step.
2: * Task search and shortcuts - Search a defined set of tasks, see your saved task changes separately from recently opened module settings, and jump between six available related workspaces. This is not a search of every Booster setting and does not link every settings screen.
3: * Invoice guide - Set up invoices in a guided flow and review a synthetic sample. The sample uses no invoice number, sends no email and does not check legal or tax requirements.
4: * Product and checkout inputs - Separate guided flows: a product input collects an answer for each product cart item and order line, a checkout field collects one answer per order, and a priced product add-on is set up on its own.
5: * Gateway fees - Set up a payment gateway fee in a guided flow. Full fee settings remain in the module.
6: * Returns - Set a storewide return window in a guided flow. Approving a request records your decision; it does not refund money, restock products or process a payment.
7: * Payment rules - Limit bank transfer (BACS) by billing country or cart amount in guided flows. Other gateway rules stay in the module settings.
8: * Shared product tab - Create one shared product tab with a guided flow.
9: * Shipping - Work through supported shipping settings in a guided flow and edit shipping method description text. The text task does not change rates or turn methods on.
10: * Button and price labels - Edit Place order and Add to cart text, price prefix and suffix, and free price text.
11: * Catalog tasks - Guided tasks for breadcrumbs, cross-sells, product images, listings, swatches, products per page, related products, sorting and upsells. Storefront results depend on the module, your theme and your configuration.
12: * Wording tasks - Edit the order notes label, placeholder and description; the currency symbol; sale badge text; and the My Account Orders label and heading. These change text only. They do not change currency conversion, taxes, sale prices, account endpoints or permissions.
13: * Percentage discounts - Edit an existing percentage discount within a limited guide. Not every pricing combination is covered.
14: * Documents and communications - New workspaces group document and email settings with help on the same screen, including limited email subject editing and guidance on recipients and consent. Booster does not confirm email delivery or scheduled task timing.
15: * Abandoned cart emails - In automated abandoned-cart email body text, the %admin_email% placeholder now uses the site administrator email from your WordPress settings instead of a fixed example address. If that setting is missing, empty or not stored as text, the placeholder is left blank. Booster does not check whether the address is valid. This changes body text only. It does not change recipients, the From address, scheduling, consent or coupons, and it does not confirm that email is delivered.
16: * Specialized selling - A label task and help for existing booking settings. This does not add subscriptions or guarantee revenue or capacity.
17: * Catalog administration - Two new tasks. Admin toolbar category links sets a global preference for category links in the admin toolbar; the Admin Bar module and WooCommerce menu prerequisites must already be in place, and the task does not activate them. Fill missing purchase costs adds costs to up to 20 distinct, explicitly selected simple products, with a preview and an Undo for that task only when its recovery checks allow. The existing SKU, Product Bulk Meta Editor, Bulk Price Converter and Admin Orders and Products List tools keep their full editors with expanded help; they do not gain new preview or Undo.
18: * CSV download - Download a CSV from up to 20 non-blank ID entries. Duplicate and invalid entries are counted, and blank separators are ignored. Every file includes ID and Status. Published items are included by default; non-public items are included only when you explicitly choose them. Booster does not import, send, schedule or store the file on the site.
19: * Diagnostics and customization - Help in existing settings, inspection of saved old-slug history records, and metadata title tools. Old-slug inspection does not test redirects or create URLs.
20: * Help and guides - Adds help inside the existing full General and role settings (these are not new guided tasks).
21: * Security - Hardens processing of untrusted product description content and date format output in affected editions. Install 10.0.0 only once it is officially released, and test it on a staging site first.
22: * Edition scope - The free edition includes the guided tasks above. Booster Plus and Booster Elite add more options. Existing module and edition limits still apply, and full module settings remain available.
23: * Compatibility - Checkout Blocks and HPOS support stays module-specific. This release does not certify every block, gateway, theme, integration, subscription service or PHP version.
24: * Hosting requirements - Requires PHP 7.3 or later on a 64-bit build with native integer hrtime() enabled. Use a maintained PHP release supported by your WordPress and WooCommerce versions.
27: * Settings backups - Export saved Booster settings and restore them after reinstalling the same edition, including general options and grouped settings.
28: * Checkout file uploads - Fix uploads with mixed-case file extensions and supported session settings. Keep staged files recoverable when an order attachment cannot be saved.
29: * Customer Return Requests - Turn on Return Requests to let signed-in customers request eligible item quantities from completed orders, follow their history and see your decision there. Verified guest access is a separate setup that needs HTTPS. Approval records your decision; it does not refund money, restock products or process a payment.
30: * Checkout Blocks - Collect supported checkout file uploads and show your Place order button text in the WooCommerce Checkout block, alongside existing supported custom fields. Existing module and edition limits still apply; this does not make every Booster option or third-party checkout compatible.
31: * Order and payment reliability - Use WooCommerce order data in affected HPOS exports and reports. Keep Booster gateway fees in sync when an eligible unpaid order changes payment method, without replacing unrelated custom fees.
32: * Understand gateway fees - See why a configured fee applies to a sample guest purchase, and check a summary of your latest up to 50 return requests. These read-only views do not change a shopper cart or predict the final checkout total. Booster Elite adds role and product facts, fee comparisons and payment/shipping rule scenarios.
33: * Hosting requirements - Requires PHP 7.3 or later on a 64-bit build with native integer hrtime() enabled. Use a maintained PHP release supported by your WordPress and WooCommerce versions.
35: * Store updates, without dashboard clutter - Receive short Booster news only on Booster settings pages. Each user can permanently dismiss a notice; store and checkout settings are unchanged.
38: * Wishlist control - Choose to keep saved products after adding them to the cart. Removal remains enabled by default, including after upgrade; disable "Remove from wishlist after adding to cart" to preserve items. Explicit removal still works.
39: * Shipping setup - Clearer guidance shows how separate category and minimum-order free-shipping methods can offer either route without duplicate free options. Existing shipping rules are not changed automatically.
40: * Security - Strengthened handling of customer-supplied product details and document processing to help keep stores protected. Updating is recommended.
41: * Branded document setup - Enter plain business details and an optional supported local logo, open a real synthetic sample, and review exact setting changes before enabling the chosen operation.
42: * Edition scope - The Light guide supports the Invoice document type, generated manually or on completed orders, with optional attachment to the customer completed-order email.
43: * Merchant control - Sample and attachment rehearsal do not send email, issue production documents or consume invoice numbers. Existing numbering, tax, advanced settings and custom templates are protected; settings undo detects later changes.
44: * Dutch continuity - Adds reviewed Dutch translations across selected core modules and the new setup guide, with English fallback outside the bounded coverage. Merchant-authored content and saved PDF templates are not translated; community and custom language overrides retain priority.
45: * Clear limits - The starter layout needs no HTML editing, but custom layouts remain in advanced settings. Sample success and attachment rehearsal do not confirm production email delivery or tax/legal compliance.
46: * Storefront continuity - Keeps setup redirects out of customer background requests after activation, so saved-list actions can work immediately.
